carouselData.alt: A child's drawing of a lorry using bath crayons.
carouselData.labelEditorState: On a steamy window or foam in the bath.

carouselData.alt: There is some gloop on a highchair tray table, and you can see a toddler's hand playing with the gloop.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Gloop - Mix up some water and cornflour to make a thick gloop - dribble it through your fingers and watch how it leaves a trail.

carouselData.alt: A ball of play dough with dents in it, made by poking with a finger.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Playdough or cake mixture - prodding or stirring.

carouselData.alt: A child using a stick to draw in sand.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Sand, soil or mud in a shallow tray or outside, making shapes using fingers, spoons, sticks etc.

carouselData.alt: A child using a thick brush to paint black marks on a white page.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Paint - thickened with flour for making finger marks, or runnier to use with brushes or sponges.

carouselData.alt: A toddler is holding a green crayon in their fist and drawing marks on a sheet of paper.
carouselData.labelEditorState: A box of paper, card and crayons - for very young children, big paper is easiest - scrap paper or the inside of cereal packets are great.

steps.editorState:
Making marks is fun but also helps children: 

  • Develop their big and small arm and hand movements needed for writing;
  • Learn to handle objects to make marks;
  • Enjoy sensory play;
  • Realise that they can make marks that mean something to them - the earliest writing.

text: Mark making noticed by Peep families

steps.editorState:
Here are a few examples of mark making noticed by Peep families:

  • Dripping water on the sofa and rubbing it in
  • Smearing hands on the mirror
  • Chalking on cupboards
  • Using pens and pencils
  • Smearing food with fingers and hands
  • Making handprints on a steamed up window
  • Dripping milk from a cup and spreading it with fingers
  • Rubbing face cream on her tummy
  • Putting deodorant on her arm
  • Mixing and spreading sand and soil on the patio
  • Walking in puddles and looking at their footprints
  • Watching their shadow and making it move
  • Putting bubbles on the side of the bath
  • Flicking water on the bathroom wall
  • Drawing with bath crayons
  • Icing cakes and biscuits

steps.text: A biscuit decorated with chocolate icing and coloured sprinkles. The decorations have clearly been done by a preschool-aged child.
